newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France says it may buy Boeing 777 planes.
newsitem.headline: Air France says it may buy Boeing 777 planes.

text.p: The chairman of French state-owned airline Air France was quoted Thursday as saying the company may buy Boeing 777 planes instead of aircraft from its traditional supplier Airbus.
In an interview with the Les Echos newspaper, Christian Blanc said: "Airbus is a formidable success and an exemplary European company. For Air France it is the standard plane maker."

But he added that the airline was making comparisons and calculations for its fleet acquisitions, which it could resume after having bought no planes since 1993 as its financial crises forced it to cut spending.
"Today, like yesterday, we need both Airbus and Boeing. Contrary to rumours circulating these past few weeks, our acquisition programme is balanced and involves both plane makers."
A board meeting is scheduled for Nov. 20 to discuss expansion of the long-range fleet.

Blanc said he did not expect opposition from the French government if the board decided to take Boeing 777 planes as well as additional Airbus A340s, such as the stretched Airbus A340-600, for which it could be the launch customer.
Transport Minister Anne-Marie Idrac declined to say in an interview with RTL radio whether the government would oppose a decision to buy Boeing planes.
